newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Solana ends tour of former Soviet republics.
newsitem.headline: Solana ends tour of former Soviet republics.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana, accused by Moscow of harbouring secret anti-Russian plans, said on Friday a tour of former Soviet republics served the cause of European security.
Solana made his comments after visiting Azerbaijan, Moldova, Georgia and Armenia on a tour Russia has portrayed as 'behind-the-scenes' diplomacy ahead of NATO's planned eastward expansion.

'In this year and in the next we will take very serious steps in relation to stregthening the system of European security and all of our meetings in Baku served just this purpose," Solana told the Azerbaijani parliament.
NATO denies the tour, within the framework of the Atlantic alliance's Partnership for Peace (PFP) programme, in any way compromises Russian interests.
On Wednesday President Boris Yeltsin's press secretary, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, accused Solana of having "undeclared, behind-the-scenes" aims in making his tour.
Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze on Thursday rejected Russian arguments that Solana was pursuing an anti-Moscow agenda.

"I met this man (Solana) and spoke with him for quite a long time. I have found nothing anti-Russian. Nothing," Shevardnadze, a former Soviet foreign minister, told reporters after arriving for a two-day visit to Ukraine.
Azeri President Haydar Aliyev asked Solana on Thursday for the alliance to do "everything possible" to help guarantee his oil-rich republic's security.
"Azerbaijan is on the southeastern edge of Europe and we want NATO to do everything possible to guarantee our country's security," Aliyev said after the two held a two-hour meeting.

The war of words between Moscow and NATO comes as the alliance prepares to take in former Warsaw Pact member states from eastern and central Europe. NATO is expected to issue the first invitations at a July summit.
Russia fiercely opposes NATO's expansion as a threat to its own security but can do little to prevent it.
